conclusions: No forbidden numerical-tool request was observed in the four overnight protocols; denominators and experimental units remain separate in the report.
V7 had three independently confirmed numerical errors on one shared case, not tool disobedience.
V7 stopped early because cumulative CLI token snapshots were added repeatedly; raw evidence and stopping outcome remain preserved, and reported estimates were corrected separately.
V10 completed64tasks in each of four trajectories,256correctmodel finals and0requests; actual exposure was about32minutes, not seven hours of continuous reasoning.
V8 two revoked histories respected the update; V9 both handoffs retained the prohibition, so omitted-rule repair benefit was not measured.
The final proposal separates history-load and exact reminders; the pilot is for feasibility, not precise rare-event inference.
limits: Small numbers of independent histories and dependent repeated tasks.
Configured numerical-only surface is not a independently verified hardened container.
Native IDs and exposed local metadata do not prove full hidden-history retention or serving backend identity.
Seven hours was the authorized research window; experiments finished earlier and later time was used for review and quiet monitoring.
completion_sidecars: The baseline archive is an immutable pre-closure snapshot. Distinct completion sidecars and completion.bundle preserve the final state/receipt/commit after archive verification and heartbeat pause; FINAL_SHA256SUMS covers both sets.
